questions.question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

There was an gang of thieves spotted at our local bank, make sure to be careful.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The primary issue in the sentence is the use of the article **"an"** before a word beginning with a consonant sound ("gang").
 
• The correct article to use in this context is** "a"** instead of **"an"**.
 
• The correct phrase should be "There was a gang", ensuring grammatical correctness and clarity.
 
• Thus, the error is located in **Option 2** of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"There was** a** gang of thieves spotted at our local bank, make sure to be careful."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "of thieves spotted"** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **Option 3: "at our local bank"** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **Option 4: "make sure to be careful"** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.

questions.question:

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

__
 
• The primary issue in the sentence is the incorrect verb form "**look**" instead of "**looked**."
 
• In** past tense **narratives, the verb should be in the past form.
 
• The correct phrase should be "**she looked up**," ensuring grammatical correctness and clarity.
 
• Thus, the error is located in **part 1** of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"After a while, she** looked up **and saw that it was getting dark."*

• **it was getting dark.** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.

questions.question:
Select the option that will improve the given sentence by using the most appropriate verb.

Alexa have being working as a teacher for five years now.

options.text: Alexa has being working as a teacher for five years now.
Alexa has been working as a teacher for five years now.
Alexa was been working as a teacher for five years now
Alexa is being working as a teacher for five years now.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The primary issue in the sentence is the incorrect use of the verb form.
 
• The correct form is **"has been working," **indicating the present perfect continuous tense.
 
• The appropriate verb phrase clarifies that Alexa has been continuously working as a teacher for five years up to the present moment.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Alexa** has been working** as a teacher for five years now."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "has being" is incorrect; the correct form is "has been."
 
• **Option 3:** "was been" is incorrect; it should be "has been" for present perfect continuous tense.
 
• **Option 4:** "is being" is incorrect; this structure does not fit the context needing the present perfect continuous tense.
